note: Advisories describe what a source *claims*. SymPort tests none of them on a phone and does not exploit anything. A pattern match is a lead; no match is not proof of safety.

advisories.title: Delight CFW: startup scripts injected through a text file in the Data directory
advisories.cwe: CWE-77 (assigned by the CISA ADP container)

severity.author_claim: The researcher's write-up calls it critical; that wording is the author's, not the scored severity.

sources.label: Researcher write-up (author's claims, not verified by SymPort)

affected.source: write-up only (not in the CVE text)

advisories.platform: Symbian Belle custom firmware. Not S60 3rd Edition: this does not describe the E52, E72 or N95.
advisories.mechanism: Claimed: a plain-text file in the user-writable data directory is read early at boot and its lines act as startup commands; no validation or user confirmation (author claim).
mitigation_claimed: Author's write-up: delete the file from the data directory and avoid applications that create it.
Author's write-up: a permanent fix would read the file only from the Z: drive; the write-up says the developer declined.
caveats: The CVE text names ':\Data'; the write-up names 'E:\Data'.
Affected versions are only in the CVE description text; the vendor field is 'n/a'.
The vendor page referenced by the CVE could not be read (bot verification).

rules.title: Binary refers to the Delight startup text file
rules.reliability: A string in a binary is a lead. It does not show that the file is read, executed or exploitable.

rules.title: Binary refers to a text file in the data directory of a writable drive
rules.reliability: Many programs name their own files. Review in context; this only highlights trust in a user-writable path.

rules.title: Reference to domainsrv (an early-start server named in autostart claims)
rules.reliability: The name appears in the standard system too; informational only.
